content:
Rumors suggest Apple will release new products on October 13. Based on the timing of recent October events, here's when Apple might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

While the timing of Apple's September events has been relatively consistent, October events are far less regular than September events—whether it's the date itself or how far in advance it's announced, it's quite difficult to predict.

Apple has only held ten October events since 2010, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Here's how far in advance Apple has announced each October event since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple plans to launch the long-rumored smart home hub, the next-generation HomePod mini, and an Apple TV 4K with a new AI-powered Siri on Tuesday, October 13—though the report did not say whether Apple would hold an event to unveil these products.

If true, Apple could announce the event date as early as Monday, October 5, or as late as Wednesday, October 7.

Also worth noting is that Apple is expected to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, a new iPad Air, a new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models in 2026—including a model with a touchscreen. As for whether some of these products will be unveiled at the same event, another event, or simply via press release, remains to be seen.

Looking back, in October 2024, Apple released new Mac products via press releases for three consecutive days; and in October 2025, Apple launched the M5 chip and all-new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models without holding an event.

In contrast, Apple has only held one November event, and that was in November 2020, when the "One More Thing" event saw the debut of the first Macs powered by M1 Apple Silicon.

Of course, 2020 was an extraordinary year for Apple's event schedule—WWDC was unusually delayed until late June, and with COVID-19 disrupting the normal schedule, Apple ended up holding events in both September and October.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at its rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
